start.speaker: gran
start.text: On a winter evening the family sits round the lamp with tea. Grandmother raises a glass: "We play the verse chain. Each line must begin with the last letter of the line before it. Will you join me?"

choices.text: Yawn, and ask for the sweets before the game
Say you will try, and ask her to open
Pour her tea first, then take your seat and ask her to open

r1.speaker: gran
r1.verse: Tea steams in the glass beside the sleeping cat
r1.text: Grandmother opens the game: "Tea steams in the glass beside the sleeping cat" It ends on the letter T.

puzzle.prompt: Pick the line that begins with T.
options: A pomegranate splits and the evening laughs
Tall poplars bow to a quiet wind
Bread is warm and the lamp is low

r2.speaker: gran
r2.verse: Dates and walnuts wait for the guest at the door
r2.text: Your line ended on D, so she answers: "Dates and walnuts wait for the guest at the door" It ends on the letter R.

puzzle.prompt: Pick the line that begins with R.
options: Rain is a letter the roof reads aloud

hint.speaker: uncle
hint.text: Uncle leans over and whispers the first letters of the next lines into your ear. Grandmother raises an eyebrow and waits.

choices.text: Take the whispered help and use it
Smile and wave it away: your own memory will do

r3.speaker: gran
r3.verse: Daylight folds itself like a shawl
r3.text: Your line ended on D again, so she goes on: "Daylight folds itself like a shawl" It ends on the letter L.

puzzle.prompt: Pick the line that begins with L.
options: Snow is a page nobody has read
Stars come out for the sleepless
Lanterns hang in the orchard's dark

r4.speaker: gran
r4.verse: Kites rise over the old roofs, full of longing
r4.text: Your line ended on K. Grandmother smiles and sets the hardest letter: "Kites rise over the old roofs, full of longing" It ends on the letter G.

puzzle.prompt: Pick the line that begins with G.
options: Quiet nights are a kind of answer
Geese go over the glass-blue hill
Ink is the shadow a poem leaves

close.speaker: gran
close.text: The tea has gone cool and the lamp burns low. Grandmother says: "A chain is only as long as its last player. How shall we end?"

choices.text: Declare yourself the champion and ask for applause
Offer her your best line and ask for hers to close the chain
Say nothing, and finish the tea

end_proud.text: Grandmother nods politely and starts to tidy the glasses. The chain is broken and so is the mood.

end_quiet.text: You sip your tea. The chain lies quiet on the page, unfinished, and the lamp flickers.

end_best.text: Her last line answers yours, and the whole family claps. The chain on the page is long, and nobody wants to be the one who ends it.

endings.headline: The chain is unbroken
endings.text: Every line found its letter and the room was kind.

endings.headline: A good evening of verse
endings.text: A few lines slipped, but the game went on.
